findings.title: Two Pachacamac accounts joined on a Huacho khipu
findings.summary: Six fragments sewn on the Basel cloth IVc.366.03 (dug near Huacho, bought 1910) repeat runs of two Berlin khipus labelled Pachacamac: UR212 (37 of 195 pendants) and AS131 (25 of 146). UR212 and AS131 each have 14 main groups, divided 7 + 7 at the same point. Every fragment that carries both khipus pairs the same unit (units 1, 4 and 14), so the Huacho khipu set the two halves of one 14-unit account side by side, 14 + 10 cords per unit.
evidence: Other khipus with ≥ 100 pendants match at most 4 cords (median 0).
Same unit in 3 of 3 fragments: p ≈ (1/14)² ≈ 0.005.
Where Berlin leaves a colour-marked cord knotless, the Basel copy carries a value (3 of 3); other knotless cords stay knotless.
Unit totals of UR212 and AS131 are not correlated (ρ = 0.19): different categories of the same units.

findings.title: A 14-unit frame in Gretzer's Berlin batch
findings.summary: Fourteen main groups are rare (1.6% of khipus outside the Berlin 'Pachacamac' batch) but occur on 4 of 23 khipus of that batch: UR212, AS131, AS170 and UR199. Berlin catalogue records describe three more that are not digitized: VA 42513 (14 × 13 pendants), VA 42537 (14 × 9) and VA 42532 (7 × A, 7 × B, 7 × A, 7 × B). AS131, UR212 and AS170 split their units 7 + 7 at the same place, each marked differently: a larger space, a single knotless cord, a marker.
evidence: Binomial P ≈ 0.0005 with all four; P ≈ 0.04 without the two khipus that prompted the question.
Across 109 OKR khipus with an even number of main groups, the largest space falls in the middle 12.9 times (13.0 expected): equal halves are not a general habit.

findings.title: Inkawasi UR269: five supply streams, each with its own deduction
findings.summary: In blocks of five records [gross, net, deduction] the deduction is 47, 46, 46, 44, 25 by place, whatever the deposit size. The place-1 records are deliveries of the stream recorded in full on UR275 (deduction 47 throughout) and its copy UR266: 5 of 10 place-1 records reappear on UR275, at one fixed offset (block b of UR269 = entry b + 15 of UR275), while places 2–5 are found on no other khipu. Each block is one round of five streams in a fixed order, each stream with its own fixed deduction. Urton & Chu (2015, 2018, 2019) list UR269 as having no repeating value. The five place deductions add up to 208, the fixed deduction of UR268, but no record-level link was found.
evidence: 33 of 43 deductions equal their place value; 17 when records are shuffled within blocks (p ≈ 0.0005).
Place 1 on UR275: 5 of 10 records (0.5 expected); places 2–4: 0, 1, 1. All five at one offset; 5,000 permutations of block order reach at most 4 (p ≈ 0.0002).
UR269 keeps the arithmetic where UR275 slips: 1827 = 1780 + 47 on UR269, 1825 on UR275.
No other Inkawasi khipu shows a place dependence (all p > 0.8).

findings.title: Inkawasi: empty slots, totals-only copies, product labels
findings.summary: On UR255 the net pendant is empty in the first 12 deposits and filled with the values of UR267A in 5 of the last 6. The bundle UR273A + UR273B records only the deposit totals of UR274A + UR274B: 4 and 6 shared totals (0.3 and 0.5 expected), in the same order on both. Copies lie in a different bundle from their counterparts. A red tassel at the start of the primary cord occurs only on peanut khipus (2 of 4 against 0 of 25).
evidence: Split this clean under random placement: about 1 in 3,900.
UR273B ~ UR274B: Poisson p ≈ 10⁻⁵.
UR273A ~ UR274A: 891, 453, 448, 448 in the same order (p ≈ 3 × 10⁻⁴); UR273B ~ UR274B: six totals in the same order (p ≈ 10⁻⁵).

findings.title: Folded copies
findings.summary: In two independent cases a separate cord in one copy is a subsidiary in the other: UR270 → UR278 at Inkawasi and UR053C → UR053B in the Waterfall set. The packing rule is ours; the near-duplication of B and C was noted by Chirinos.
evidence: UR053B/C: 35 fields match against at most 18 in 2,000 shuffles.

findings.title: Two Dumbarton Oaks khipus transcribed
findings.summary: UR297 (438 pendants, 623 cords) and UR298 (203 pendants, 285 cords), given by Bill Conklin, exist in the OKR only as scans of Urton's handwritten sheets. We transcribed all 65 pages. 74 of the 78 group totals Urton noted on the sheets equal ours. UR297 has 41 groups, mostly ten cords plus one summary cord pulled up like a top cord. Neither khipu is linked to any other.

compare.title: Check against Urton's own totals
compare.text: On the last eight sheets of UR297 Urton wrote the total of each group and of its summary cord: 78 totals in all. 74 of the 78 equal our transcription (do_check.py).

negatives.title: Summary khipus
negatives.text: No khipu records the group totals or column sums of another beyond chance (384 pairs against 415.6 on the offset baseline).

negatives.title: Compilations
negatives.text: Apart from the Basel fragments, no khipu combines runs from two or more other khipus.

negatives.title: Colonial documents
negatives.text: About 2,300 numbers from roughly 70 open transcriptions match no digitized khipu.

negatives.title: Huacones-Vilcahuasi hierarchy
negatives.text: Totals of one khipu on the next are at the level of chance (offset baseline).

negatives.title: Opposite attachment in copies
negatives.text: Recto on one copy and verso on the other in 7 of 10 pairs, against 50% at random (p ≈ 0.17).

negatives.title: Same suppliers in the same order
negatives.text: Deposit sizes of different Inkawasi khipus do not correlate by position.

negatives.title: Copies respect group boundaries
negatives.text: Run endpoints fall on group boundaries in 38% of cases against 46% expected.

negatives.title: Broken cords as lower bounds
negatives.text: Sums with a broken part are exact half as often (35% vs 68%), but the sign shows no loss of knots.

negatives.title: Equal-share convention
negatives.text: Pairs of equal-total groups are not over-represented corpus-wide (p ≈ 0.1).

negatives.title: Pachacamac style vs Huacho style
negatives.text: Simple numeric features do not separate site-museum Pachacamac khipus from Huacho khipus.

negatives.title: Sign convention
negatives.text: Neither attachment side nor colour marks negative cords.

negatives.title: Syllables in non-decimal khipus
negatives.text: The non-decimal signs of Wari-style khipus have far too small an alphabet for syllables.

negatives.title: Calendar reading
negatives.text: Group and cord counts give no calendar numbers beyond chance.

negatives.title: Colour of the product
negatives.text: Colour is not carried into copies and does not mark the product at Inkawasi.

negatives.title: Ordered totals and strided copies
negatives.text: Group totals of one khipu repeated in the same order on another (192 khipus with at least three non-round totals ≥ 100): every pair above the shifted-value baseline is a copy already known or a second recording of one object. Within Inkawasi, every p-th record of one khipu laid against consecutive records of another (strides 2–8): only UR269 ~ UR275 stands out; the rest is at the level expected from the number of strides and offsets tried.

timeline.title: Inka period
timeline.text: Most khipus of the corpus date to the Inka period; radiocarbon dates, where tested, fall here.

timeline.title: Huanca lords record what they gave the Spaniards
timeline.text: Their khipus, read out in court, keep the shares of the valley's three parts, 4 : 2 : 3 (Chirinos 2010).

timeline.title: A summary khipu equals twelve detail khipus
timeline.text: Hatun Xauxa's summary of 1558 is the sum of the detail khipus shown in 1561 (Chirinos 2010). No such pair survives in the corpus.

timeline.title: Third Council of Lima
timeline.text: The council orders khipus to be destroyed; the court record of khipu readings ends soon after.

timeline.title: Wilhelm Gretzer arrives in Peru
timeline.text: A textile merchant from Hanover, he builds the largest collection of its time, mostly from grave robbers.

timeline.title: Macedo collection to Berlin
timeline.text: Berlin buys about 2,400 objects from José Mariano Macedo of Lima.

timeline.title: Eduard Gaffron practises medicine in Lima
timeline.text: His collection later reaches Berlin (the Huacho khipus VA 63038–63044), Detmold and other museums.

timeline.title: Max Uhle excavates at Pachacamac
timeline.text: The first systematic excavation of the sanctuary.

timeline.title: Baessler gift
timeline.text: Arthur Baessler gives Berlin about 11,690 objects.

timeline.title: Khipus 'between Ica and Pisco' reach Berlin
timeline.text: Among them AS114, whose block recurs on AS123.

timeline.title: Berlin buys Gretzer's collection
timeline.text: About 40,000 objects, most labelled Pachacamac, among them UR212, AS131, AS170 and AS175.

timeline.title: The Ica khipus AS143, AS149, AS179 enter Berlin
timeline.text: One allocation spread over three khipus of the same batch.

timeline.title: Gaffron khipus in Detmold
timeline.text: Entered with other objects from his collection.

timeline.title: Basel buys khipus dug near Huacho
timeline.text: The ship's doctor Arnold Masarey sells a cache of cords; the museum's report calls them calendar records.

timeline.title: Nordenskiöld mounts the Huacho khipus
timeline.text: Ten fragments and loose cords are sewn onto a cloth, IVc.366.03, and pieces face both ways.

timeline.title: Nordenskiöld's calendar reading
timeline.text: He publishes the calendar hypothesis but not the Basel khipus.

timeline.title: The Aschers' Databooks
timeline.text: Cord-by-cord records of more than 200 khipus, with observations such as the 7 + 7 parts of AS131 and AS170.

timeline.title: Inkawasi storehouse excavated
timeline.text: Alejandro Chu recovers 34 khipus, some under chili peppers, peanuts and black beans.

timeline.title: Urton & Chu on Inkawasi
timeline.text: Matched pairs and fixed deductions 10, 15, 47, 208.

timeline.title: Conklin khipus at Dumbarton Oaks
timeline.text: UR297 and UR298 enter the collection.

timeline.title: Huacones-Vilcahuasi
timeline.text: Eleven khipus found rolled together near a chili storeroom and a floor yupana.

timeline.title: Medrano traces the Basel khipus to Huacho
timeline.text: The museum archive names the burial ground near Huacho and the 1924 mounting.

timeline.title: This atlas
timeline.text: Corpus-wide search: every link between surviving khipus is a copy of one account.
